source.title: Zašto je hrvatska politika tako DOSADNA? - Jak EGO, slabe IDEJE | JAKOV ŽIŽIĆ #PODCAST 119

summary.title_hr: Zašto je hrvatska politika tako DOSADNA? - Jak EGO, slabe IDEJE | JAKOV ŽIŽIĆ #PODCAST 119
summary.abstract_hr: U 119. epizodi podcasta udruge Mladi za Domovinu voditelj razgovara s politologom Jakovom Žižićem s Hrvatskog katoličkog sveučilišta, kolumnistom Glasa Koncila, o političkim ideologijama i njihovoj ulozi u hrvatskoj politici. Žižić objašnjava podjelu ideologija na monističke, pluralističke i slabo utemeljene. Upozorava da su se velike stranke previše približile i postale varijante vladajuće liberalne paradigme. Ističe i da se hrvatski birači ideološki dijele prema odnosu prema Crkvi i povijesti, a ne prema socijalno-ekonomskim pitanjima. Razgovor analizira ideološke profile HDZ-a, SDP-a, Možemo!, Mosta, Domovinskog pokreta i Domina, institucionalni konzervatizam te 'egokraciju' Andreja Plenkovića i Zorana Milanovića. Završava se procjenama mogućih izbornih kombinacija, posebno uspona Tomislava Tomaševića i Igora Štimca, te pozivom da se više raspravlja o ulozi države umjesto o prošlosti.
key_topics: štrajk u zagrebačkom holdingu i čistoći
key_points: Žižić ideologije opisuje kao 'zemljovid u politici': pomažu u snalaženju i tumačenju političkih pojava, određuju za što se zalažemo i povezuju politiku s građanima. Stranke koje tvrde da nemaju ideologiju često zastupaju tehnokraciju, koja je i sama ideologija.

Prema njegovoj ocjeni, demokršćanstvo, socijaldemokracija, liberalizam i progresivne opcije previše su se približili i postali stranačke varijante vladajuće liberalne paradigme. Kao posljedicu navodi nestajanje FDP-a u Njemačkoj.
U Hrvatskoj se birači ideološki ne dijele prema ekonomskim pitanjima, nego prema odnosu prema Crkvi i prema povijesti. Socijalno-ekonomska pitanja zato nisu politički relevantna pri glasovanju.

Plenkovića smatra ideološki neprofiliranim političarem čiju dugovječnost objašnjava europskom legitimacijom, kontrolom kadrova i vještim upravljanjem koalicijama. Pripisuje mu institucionalni konzervatizam, primjerice inzistiranje na postojećem modelu izbora ustavnih sudaca.

Štrajk u zagrebačkom holdingu i čistoći po Žižiću je pokazao koliko je tržišna logika prodrla u društvo. Ljudi su reagirali kao potrošači, a ne kao solidarni članovi zajednice. Možemo! naziva liberalnom, a ne ljevičarskom strankom čije biračko tijelo nije klasično radništvo.
Pojmom 'politička egokracija' opisuje dominaciju i sukob Plenkovića i Milanovića. Taj sukob dijelom pripisuje polupredsjedničkom sustavu koji predsjedniku ostavlja dio izvršnih ovlasti.

Tomislava Tomaševića vidi kao najizglednijeg kandidata SDP-a i Možemo! za predsjednika Vlade, a Igora Štimca kao mogućeg okupljača usitnjene desnice, uz otvoreno pitanje tko će mu osigurati infrastrukturu i financiranje.
key_topics_en: strike in Zagrebački holding and Čistoća
key_points_en: Žižić describes ideologies as a 'map in politics': they help in finding one's way and interpreting political phenomena, determine what we stand for, and connect politics with citizens. Parties that claim to have no ideology often advocate technocracy, which is itself an ideology.

According to his assessment, Christian democracy, social democracy, liberalism, and progressive options have drawn too close to each other and become party variants of the ruling liberal paradigm. As a consequence, he cites the disappearance of the FDP in Germany.

In Croatia, voters are not ideologically divided according to economic issues, but according to their attitude toward the Church and toward history. Socio-economic issues are therefore not politically relevant in voting.

He considers Plenković an ideologically unprofiled politician whose longevity he explains by European legitimation, cadre control, and skillful management of coalitions. He attributes institutional conservatism to him, for example insisting on the existing model for the election of constitutional judges.

The strike in Zagrebački holding and Čistoća, according to Žižić, showed how much market logic has penetrated society. People reacted as consumers, rather than as supportive members of a community. He calls Možemo! a liberal, rather than a leftist party whose electorate is not the classical working class.

With the term 'political egocracy' he describes the dominance and conflict between Plenković and Milanović. He partly attributes that conflict to the semi-presidential system that leaves part of executive powers to the president.

He sees Tomislav Tomašević as the most likely candidate of SDP and Možemo! for Prime Minister, and Igor Štimac as a potential unifier of the fragmented right, with the open question of who will provide him with infrastructure and financing.

summary.title_en: Why is Croatian Politics so BORING? - Strong EGO, Weak IDEAS | JAKOV ŽIŽIĆ #PODCAST 119
summary.abstract_en: In the 119th episode of the podcast of the association Mladi za Domovinu, the host talks with political scientist Jakov Žižić from the Catholic University of Croatia, a columnist for Glas Koncila, about political ideologies and their role in Croatian politics. Žižić explains the division of ideologies into monistic, pluralistic, and weakly grounded. He warns that the major parties have drawn too close to each other and become variants of the ruling liberal paradigm. He also emphasizes that Croatian voters are ideologically divided according to their attitude toward the Church and history, rather than along socio-economic issues. The conversation analyzes the ideological profiles of HDZ, SDP, Možemo!, Most, Domovinski pokret, and Domino, institutional conservatism, and the 'egocracy' of Andrej Plenković and Zoran Milanović. It concludes with assessments of potential electoral combinations, especially the rise of Tomislav Tomašević and Igor Štimac, and a call for more debate on the role of the state instead of the past.
